diagrams.title: From Mining Rig to AI Rental Rig
diagrams.subtitle: Five operator steps before a card earns rental income

stages.label: Test the used GPU in person
stages.detail: Test before paying, price-check on gpudeals.net, seat the 12V cable fully and run a 14-gauge power cable.

stages.label: Size power at 80% load
stages.detail: PSUs, PDUs and rack circuits sized to sit at a consistent 80% load.

stages.label: Stress test 48 hours to a week
stages.detail: Run the C-Payne stress tool and watch for throttling, such as a 4090 dropping from 450 W to 230 W.

stages.label: Pin the CPU clock and power floor
stages.detail: Locking a 7950X at 1600 MHz cut system draw from 600 W to 318 W; never power-limit below 90% on Salad.

stages.label: List on a rental marketplace
stages.detail: Vast takes about 25%, SimplePod 20%, Salad 10% plus 40 cents; a 4090 on Salad nets about $2.92 a day.

diagrams.caption: Operators who left crypto mining agree the money now sits in renting VRAM, and every step guards that rental income.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Step order is an editorial sequence of separate practitioner gates; fee splits and the $2.92 daily net are as reported, not recomputed.
diagrams.note: Sources: Modern Mining (WJnsgbZsg0U), Alec Glover (CgsDEFaGLJ0, iuLuDflfEE4), BearMarketMiner (egH5hKD913Y).

diagrams.title: Neocloud Utilization Thresholds
diagrams.subtitle: Where an H100 fleet stops beating broad stocks

stages.label: Full utilization
stages.detail: H100 bought for $25K plus $5K opex, rented at $2.30/hr for about 4 years.

stages.label: Workload-aware scheduler
stages.conversion: ~$150k per day ahead of default scheduling
stages.detail: Modeled on a 10,000-GPU fleet costing about $400M across 1,250 hosts in 32 racks.

stages.label: Break-even against broad stocks
stages.conversion: At or below this, broad stocks win

stages.label: Commitment gate at a 50% contract discount
stages.conversion: Sign only where utilization clears 1 minus the discount
stages.detail: Neocloud contracts run up to 30 to 50% cheaper; the commitment rule applied to the top of that range.

stages.label: Default Kubernetes scheduler
stages.detail: Default scheduling on the same 10,000-GPU model fleet.

diagrams.caption: Idle or stalled GPUs bleed money, so the scheduler decides which side of break-even a fleet lands on.
diagrams.assumptions_note: The 50% stage applies The Code Notebook's one-minus-discount rule to the TMLS 30 to 50% contract range; every other value is as reported.
diagrams.note: Sources: Caleb Writes Code (9u2hCf8FlW0), Codemia (a_zou7QahAo), The Code Notebook (IZtzUfhm8LU), Toronto Machine Learning Society (_oWJ0t-RW7o).

diagrams.title: FinOps Gates Before Committing or Repatriating
diagrams.subtitle: Four checks that keep a discount from losing money

nodes.question: Is the commitment term no longer than the workload's predicted life?
nodes.fail_action: Shorten the term; a three-year plan on a two-year app wastes a full year.

nodes.question: Are existing RIs and savings plans overlaid before right-sizing?
nodes.fail_action: Overlay first, or the downsized VM leaves the reservation underutilized.

nodes.question: Does the FinOps agent start read-only or human-in-the-loop, with keys hidden by .gitignore?
nodes.fail_action: Lock the agent to read-only and confirm .gitignore before code leaves the box.

nodes.question: For repatriation, is the used server's BMC free of a vendor cloud license, with platform documentation?
nodes.pass_next: Proceed and benchmark ESR against the 10.5% average and ~40.5% 98th percentile

diagrams.caption: Policy becomes automation and automation becomes guardrails, but only after these gates hold.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Gate order is an editorial sequence; the ESR benchmark covers more than 1,400 data points with up to $2M per month in compute spend.
diagrams.note: Sources: Intellipaat (7_L1_3-4kg8), FinOps Foundation (b7TiwS4_Ytw), AWS Events (JqwiGt78aOI), Craft Computing (JoqFD69bWLw), ProsperOps, a Flexera company (KW_LS_stgvc).

diagrams.title: Who Stands Between a Brand and Delivered SMS
diagrams.subtitle: A2P 10DLC registration, vetting and throughput

center.headcount: 1 brand per business; an agency never registers itself as the brand
center.focus: Opt-in call to action a reviewer can actually see, legal name and EIN matched to IRS records

spokes.kpi: $4 brand fee; legal name, EIN and DUNS match exactly
$40 one-time; score 80-100 unlocks 4,500 TPM and 200,000 segments/day
$15 per attempt; one MSP needed about 15 attempts
Default 2,000 segments/day T-Mobile, 75 TPM AT&T; internal caps as low as 60 per minute

diagrams.caption: Registration lives or dies on the opt-in call to action, and throughput is set by the vetting score.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Practitioners disagree on whether resubmissions cost money; Telgorithm reports $15 per DCA attempt while Austin Marland reports no repeat fee.
diagrams.note: Sources: Telgorithm (dgkKW0cbz1E), TwilioDevs (KWvbRToRnGg, 7pXYEARPIwU), RingLogix (gmCqaG2hBKQ), Paradigm Escape (wpj7_7cz4Kk), Signal House (sVsWkczKncU), Telecom Application Development Summit (SRizDef5BbE).

diagrams.title: Voice Resale Compliance Before Launch
diagrams.subtitle: Four checks that decide whether traffic gets carried

weeks.title: Confirm your own RMD listing
weeks.deliverable: Robocall Mitigation Database listing and certification verified directly
weeks.gate: Do not trust the upstream carrier or lawyer; traffic from unlisted providers is refused as of May 28, 2024

weeks.title: Verify attestation
weeks.deliverable: Call the 920-66-1392 checker from your own trunk; buy DIDs from the carrier that signs your calls
weeks.gate: Anything other than A attestation is fixed

weeks.title: File state and tax obligations
weeks.deliverable: Filed in every state with billing and tax modeled; uncollectibles entered as positive numbers
weeks.gate: No launch until filings are complete

weeks.title: Cap exposure and check margin
weeks.deliverable: Daily spend and per-minute caps on A-Z termination; USF pass-through at four to five dollars a bill
weeks.gate: Resale margin holds at 15 to 20 percent

diagrams.caption: Compliance now decides who survives in voice resale, against a margin of only 15 to 20 percent.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Weekly sequencing is an editorial ordering of practitioner gates; Sangoma, ZCorum and Crosstalk disagree on reseller STIR/SHAKEN obligations.
diagrams.note: Sources: Crosstalk Solutions (ycGPHG_ANrE), ZCorum (ZLzeR3N0mpc), Sangoma (3XJ9OkK8aFw), The Boon of Wireless (Gye5g8KT7Oo), Public Service Commission of Wisconsin (vH9VQq2V9Qw).
